prompt: A two-colour reduction linocut, rust-orange laid down first and heavy black printed over it from the same recut block, pressed onto coarse cream paper, the two inks sitting slightly out of register. There is no soft shading anywhere: every mark is a hacked, splintered gouge, raw and angry, as though carved in a hurry. We lie at gravel level on a park path in 1919, right beside the scuffed rubber foot of a wooden crutch looming huge and close in the lower left corner, and the whole view is tipped several degrees so the path climbs steeply away from us. High up and far off sits a park bench, drawn tiny and needle-sharp: a corpulent plutocrat wearing a towering stovepipe hat and a buttoned morning coat, flicking his fingers outward in a lazy brush-off, and beside him a gaunt veteran with a cropped head and a frayed khaki tunic, one leg ending at the knee, the empty trouser folded and pinned. Behind them a swollen dusk sun hangs low on the horizon, a burning orange disc with chiselled rays. From it the plutocrat's shadow spills down the path toward us, grotesquely oversized and stretched, the hat drawn out into a black chimney and the belly into a heaving blot, rearing over the seated veteran and running all the way down the gravel until it touches the crutch beside us. The veteran's shadow is only a frail cracked splinter. Leafless trees bend inward from both sides like bars. Above the bench, a wide strip of raw streaked orange sky stays completely empty. No writing, lettering, numbers or signs anywhere. Thanks.
